premises.text: Mobile teams need to work together, but email is inadequate for sharing files, talking, and calendaring as a group
premises.evidence_span: the world's gone mobile. We all need to communicate as teams. But email doesn't really cut it for us all the time

premises.text: Zula is a structured team messaging stream with embedded work tools—file sharing, polls, file library with Dropbox/Drive, calendar events, and search
premises.evidence_span: we started off with a very standard messaging stream, a structured messaging stream. And we said, OK, what do we need to add to this for business tools to really get things done together as a team?

premises.text: People are invited into streams from contacts and social networks via deep links that land them directly in the conversation
premises.evidence_span: I invite people into a stream the way I interact with people today, which is really the convergence of our social worlds and our business worlds

premises.text: One-tap conference calling from the stream rings participants with a join push and needs no phone numbers
premises.evidence_span: we have one tap conference calling

value.text: Teams get things done with less email through a structured mobile conversation workspace
value.evidence_span: this is the beginning of reducing email and moving into a much more structured way of communicating as a team

causal_links.evidence_span: when we're communicating with email, sometimes we have to share files. Sometimes we have to talk to people. Sometimes we want to calendar things
we know it really helps us get things done and obviously has way reduced our email
sometimes all of this back and forth is not enough. And all this asynchronous communication

notes: File share, polls, Dropbox/Drive library, calendar, and search folded as cascade of one structured messaging workspace (§4.1.7). Social invite/deep link kept with that collaboration surface. One-tap calling split as separately framed synchronous module when async is not enough. Six months of dogfooding treated as traction, not a premise.
